<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Implement FieldLive slice">
Implement the cleaner field app in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive live context — Today (day view), Job (job workspace), ChecklistComponent, IncidentFormComponent, EarningsComponent — with routes ~p"/field" and ~p"/field/jobs/:id" in the authenticated live_session. Mobile-first DaisyUI.

FIRST: call mcp start_task with requirement_name="implementation_file", entity_type="component", module_name="CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Today", then per component (FieldLive.Job, FieldLive.ChecklistComponent, FieldLive.IncidentFormComponent, FieldLive.EarningsComponent). If module_name isn't accepted, resolve via list_requirements module_filter="FieldLive".

BUILD ORDER: Today first (story 841 — depends only on stable Scheduling/Clients/Notifications), then Job + components.

Acceptance contracts — read ALL of: test/spex/841_*/ (day view: jobs in start-time order, only MY jobs, access code visible day-of only, full get-in-the-door brief, placeholders for missing optional details, empty-day state, updated lockbox propagates), test/spex/842_*/ (room-grouped checklist via Quality API, check-off, LiveView photo uploads, completion blocked with required unchecked, offline retry), test/spex/843_*/ (change alerts on Today requiring explicit acknowledgment), test/spex/844_*/ (clock in/out buttons, per-job earnings, pay-period total, drive-time policy; opening a job NOT assigned to you = redirect to /field with "not assigned" flash — reconciled contract, see 838/criterion_7123 and 844/criterion_7129), test/spex/845_*/ (incident form: photo required for damage/missing-item, not unsafe-condition; immutable after submit; office notified), plus 836/criterion_7153 + 839's field-driven criteria (completing a job generates invoice + quality flows).

Available context APIs (read the modules, don't reimplement): CleanerCrm.Scheduling (jobs, day queries), CleanerCrm.Clients (property access details), CleanerCrm.Quality (get_checklist_for_job/instantiate, group_by_room, toggle_checklist_item, incomplete_required_items, complete_job — gates completion and flips job status, attach_photo/complete_photo_upload, file_incident_report), CleanerCrm.TimeTracking (clock in/out, Earnings — may still be landing; read lib/cleaner_crm/time_tracking* when you get there and integrate defensively), CleanerCrm.Notifications (ack’able schedule-change notifications), CleanerCrm.Billing.generate_for_job if present (call on completion if the function exists; otherwise leave documented TODO).

Do NOT modify other agents' files: scheduling*, quality*, time_tracking*, billing*, notifications*, quoting*, client_live/*, schedule_live/*, audit* — read-only. You own only lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/* + router additions.

Verify: mix compile clean, mix format; run `mix spex` on 841, 842, 844, 845 dirs (+ spot-check 839/836 field criteria); `mix test` no regressions.

Final response: files, per-story pass counts (841/842/844/845), blockers. Under 200 words.
</teammate-message>

Project: Cleaner CRM Project Description: Component Name: Today Component Description: Day view of jobs in order with access info and change alerts requiring acknowledgment Type: liveview Test File: test/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/today_test.exs Implementation Instructions: 1. Read the test file to understand the expected behavior and any test fixtures 2. Read the linked story's BDD spex (under `test/spex/_*/`) — they are the contract for this component's public API 3. Create all necessary module files 4. Implement all public API functions implied by the spex and tests 5. Ensure the implementation satisfies the tests 6. Create schemas, migrations, or supporting code as needed Coding Rules: You are Jose Valim, creator of the Elixir Language. Write clean, functional, simple elixir code. Identify what should be separate modules. Each modules must have a single, clear responsibility. Never put multiple concerns in one modules. Replace cond with pattern matching. Replace if/else statements with pattern matching. Match on function heads, case statements, and with clauses. If you can't pattern match it, redesign the data structure. Use with blocks over multiple nested conditionals. Never modify existing data. Always return new data structures. Use the pipe operator `|>` to chain transformations. Reject any solution that requires mutable state. Validate inputs at process boundaries using guards, pattern matching, or explicit validation. Crash the process rather than propagating invalid data through the system. Separate pure functions from side effects. Use dedicated processes for I/O operations. Never hide side effects inside seemingly pure functions. Define custom types and structs that make invalid combinations impossible. Use guards and specs to enforce constraints at compile time and runtime. Processes must communicate exclusively through message passing. Never share memory or state between processes. Design clear message protocols for each interaction. Handle the Happy Path, Let Everything Else Crash. Focus code on the expected successful execution path. Don't try to handle every possible error - let the supervisor handle process failures and restarts. Write tests that verify message passing between processes and supervision behavior. Test that processes crash appropriately and recover correctly. # Collaboration Guidelines - **Challenge and question**: Don't immediately agree or proceed with requests that seem suboptimal, unclear, or potentially problematic - **Push back constructively**: If a proposed approach has issues, suggest better alternatives with clear reasoning - **Think critically**: Consider edge cases, performance implications, maintainability, and best practices before implementing - **Seek clarification**: Ask follow-up questions when requirements are ambiguous or could be interpreted multiple ways - **Propose improvements**: Suggest better patterns, more robust solutions, or cleaner implementations when appropriate - **Be a thoughtful collaborator**: Act as a good teammate who helps improve the overall quality and direction of the project # LiveView Coding Rules ## Design System Read `.code_my_spec/design/design_system.html` for the project's design system before writing any templates. Use the DaisyUI component classes and theme tokens defined there. Do not invent custom colors or component patterns that deviate from the design system. ## General When possible, include both the markup and the functions in a single .ex file, not split between an .ex file and a .html.heex file. The render function should be at the top. ## Component Hierarchy (use in this order) ### 1. Project core_components.ex (first choice) Use the function components defined in the project's `core_components.ex`. These include: `<.button>`, `<.input>`, `<.flash>`, `<.table>`, `<.header>`, `<.modal>`, `<.list>`, `<.icon>`, `<.back>`, `<.simple_form>`, `<.error>`, `<.label>`. Read core_components.ex to discover the full set before implementing. ### 2. DaisyUI component classes (second choice) When core_components doesn't cover a pattern, use DaisyUI semantic classes. Common components to reach for: - Layout: `card`, `drawer`, `navbar`, `footer`, `hero`, `divider` - Navigation: `menu`, `tabs`, `breadcrumbs`, `steps`, `bottom-navigation` - Data display: `stat`, `table`, `badge`, `kbd`, `countdown`, `diff` - Feedback: `alert`, `toast`, `loading`, `skeleton`, `progress` - Actions: `dropdown`, `swap`, `theme-controller` - Overlay: `modal`, `tooltip` Example — prefer DaisyUI: ```heex <%!-- Good: DaisyUI card --%>

<%= @title %>

<%= @description %>

<.button>Learn More
<%!-- Bad: raw Tailwind rebuilding a card from scratch --%>

<%= @title %>

<%= @description %>

<.button>Learn More
``` ### 3. Raw Tailwind utility classes (last resort) Only use raw Tailwind classes for fine-grained adjustments that DaisyUI doesn't cover, such as custom spacing, positioning, or one-off visual tweaks. You run in an environment where ast-grep is available; whenever a search requires syntax-aware or structural matching, default to ast-grep --lang elixir -p '' (or set --lang appropriately) and avoid falling back to text-only tools like rg or grep unless I explicitly request a plain-text search. defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
16	    AvailabilityBlock,
17	    ConflictDetector,
18	    Job,
19	    Recurrence,
20	    RecurringPlan
21	  }
22	
23	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User
25	
26	  ## Jobs
27	
28	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
29	    Job
30	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
31	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
32	    |> Repo.get!(id)
33	  end
34	
35	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
36	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
37	  end
38	
39	  @doc """
40	  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
41	  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
42	  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
43	  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
44	  """
45	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
46	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
47	    with {:ok, job} <-
48	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
49	           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
50	           |> Repo.insert() do
51	      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
52	      {:ok, job}
53	    end
54	  end
55	
56	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
57	    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
58	  end
59	
60	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
61	    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
62	  end
63	
64	  defp job_created_values(job) do
65	    %{"scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date), "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
66	  end
67	
68	  @doc """
69	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
70	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
71	  """
72	  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
73	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
74	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)
75	
76	    Job
77	    |> where(
78	      [j],
79	      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
80	        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
81	    )
82	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
83	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
84	    |> Repo.all()
85	  end
86	
87	  @doc """
88	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
89	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
90	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
91	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
92	  """
93	  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
94	    Job
95	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
96	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
97	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
98	    |> Repo.all()
99	  end
100	
101	  @doc """
102	  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
103	  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
104	  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
105	  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
106	  """
107	  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
108	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
109	    with :ok <-
110	           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
111	             scope,
112	             cleaner_id,
113	             job.scheduled_date,
114	             job.start_time,
115	             job.end_time,
116	             exclude_job_id: job.id
117	           ),
118	         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
119	      Recorder.record(
120	        scope,
121	        "job_reassigned",
122	        "Job",
123	        updated.id,
124	        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
125	        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
126	      )
127	
128	      {:ok, updated}
129	    end
130	  end
131	
132	  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
133	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
134	    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
135	      Recorder.record(
136	        scope,
137	        "job_cancelled",
138	        "Job",
139	        updated.id,
140	        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
141	        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
142	      )
143	
144	      {:ok, updated}
145	    end
146	  end
147	
148	  ## Recurring plans
149	
150	  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
151	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
152	    RecurringPlan
153	    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
154	    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
155	    |> Repo.get!(id)
156	  end
157	
158	  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
159	    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
160	  end
161	
162	  @doc """
163	  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
164	  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
165	  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
166	  """
167	  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
168	    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
169	  end
170	
171	  @doc """
172	  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
173	  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
174	  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
175	  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
176	  """
177	  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
178	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
179	    Repo.transact(fn ->
180	      with {:ok, plan} <-
181	             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
182	             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
183	             |> Repo.insert() do
184	        jobs =
185	          plan
186	          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
187	          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
188	            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
189	            job
190	          end)
191	
192	        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
193	      end
194	    end)
195	  end
196	
197	  ## Availability blocks
198	
199	  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
200	    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
201	  end
202	
203	  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
204	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
205	    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
206	    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
207	    |> Repo.insert()
208	  end
209	
210	  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date), "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
4	  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),

18	    Checklist,

24	  }

26	  ## Checklist templates
27

29	      when not is_nil(account_id) do

31	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
32	    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
33	    |> Repo.all()

37	      when not is_nil(account_id) do

39	    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
40	    |> Repo.get!(id)
41	  end

44	    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
45	  end

48	      when not is_nil(account_id) do

50	    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
51	    |> Repo.insert()
52	  end
53	
54	  ## Checklists

56	  @doc """
57	  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
58	  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
59	  """

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
          end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
  """
  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
  end

  @doc """
  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
  """
  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
    end
  end

  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
        {:ok, completed}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp mark_job_completed(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, job_id) do
    job = Job |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id) |> Repo.get!(job_id)

    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :completed}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_completed",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "completed"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Records the owner's 1-5 quality rating for a job, recomputing the
  checklist's combined quality score.
  """
  def rate_job(%Scope{}, %Checklist{} = checklist, rating) do
    rated = %{checklist | owner_rating: rating}

    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{owner_rating: rating, quality_score: Scorecard.score(rated)})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(
               scope,
               job,
               Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))
             ) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{
         before_photo: before_photo,
         after_photo: after_photo
       }) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    before = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    aftr = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [before, aftr]}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def complete_photo_upload(%Scope{}, %Photo{} = photo, storage_key) do
    photo |> Photo.uploaded_changeset(storage_key) |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Incident reports

  @doc """
  Files an incident report for a job. `attrs` needs `:type`
  (`"damage"`, `"missing_item"`, or `"unsafe_condition"`) and
  `:description`; a `:photo` (the same attrs `attach_photo/4` takes)
  is required unless `:type` is `"unsafe_condition"`. The cleaner and
  filing time are always the caller's and now — never accepted from
  `attrs` — and nothing about a filed report can change afterward.
  """
  def file_incident_report(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id, user: user}, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    {photo_attrs, report_attrs} = attrs |> stringify_keys() |> Map.pop("photo")

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, report} <-
             %IncidentReport{account_id: account_id}
             |> IncidentReport.changeset(
               Map.merge(report_attrs, %{
                 "job_id" => job.id,
                 "cleaner_id" => user && user.id,
                 "filed_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
               }),
               not is_nil(photo_attrs)
             )
             |> Repo.insert() do
        photo = photo_attrs && insert_incident_photo!(account_id, report, photo_attrs)
        {:ok, %{report | photos: Enum.filter([photo], & &1)}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp stringify_keys(attrs), do: Map.new(attrs, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)

  defp insert_incident_photo!(account_id, %IncidentReport{} = report, photo_attrs) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(
      Map.merge(stringify_keys(photo_attrs), %{
        "incident_report_id" => report.id,
        "kind" => "incident",
        "upload_state" => "uploaded",
        "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists an account's incident reports, most recently filed first,
  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.
  """
  def list_incident_reports(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    IncidentReport
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Scorecards

  @doc """
  The cleaner's average quality score and trend across their
  completed jobs, oldest first (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`).
  """
  def cleaner_scorecard(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> join(:inner, [c], j in Job, on: j.id == c.job_id)
    |> where(
      [c, j],
      c.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        not is_nil(c.completed_at)
    )
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.completed_at)
    |> select([c], c.quality_score)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
    |> Scorecard.aggregate()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
  @moduledoc """
  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    clocked_in_at |> DateTime.to_date() |> DateTime.new(time, time_zone)
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: Earnings.job_cents(job, entries),
        unresolved?: Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice do
  @moduledoc """
  An invoice for a completed job.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, `status` only ever advances on a Stripe
  webhook confirmation: charging a card or sending a payment link just
  submits a charge and moves the invoice to `:charge_pending`; only the
  webhook marks it `:paid`, and a declined charge reverts it to
  `:unpaid` so the owner can retry or fall back to a payment link.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type status :: :unpaid | :charge_pending | :paid

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          payment_token: String.t() | nil,
          job: CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "invoices" do
    field :amount_cents, :integer
    field :amount, :decimal, virtual: true
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :charge_pending, :paid], default: :unpaid
    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
    field :payment_token, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(job_id amount amount_cents status stripe_payment_intent_id payment_token)a

  def changeset(invoice, attrs) do
    invoice
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> put_amount_cents()
    |> validate_number(:amount_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:payment_token)
  end

  # `amount` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the money-handling
  # ADR); rounded half-up and stored as `amount_cents` — the only column
  # ever persisted. Callers that already have cents (e.g. copying a job's
  # `agreed_price_cents`) pass `amount_cents` directly and skip this.
  defp put_amount_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :amount) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :amount_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7190Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7190 — Moving a job's time on the schedule board pushes the
  reassigned cleaner a notification describing the old and new times.

  Assumes the board exposes a per-job start-time control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-start-time-input']`, `phx-change="reschedule_job"`)
  alongside the cleaner-select control already assumed by story 834's
  criterion 7170.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a moved job notifies the assigned cleaner" do
    scenario "moved job notifies the cleaner" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7192Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7192 — Acknowledging clears the pending change

  The push itself is covered end-to-end by criteria 7190/7191; this
  spec's subject is the acknowledge action, so the already-pending
  notification is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture/4`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "acknowledging a pending schedule change clears it" do
    scenario "acknowledging clears the pending change" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have a pending schedule-change notification", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today()
          })

        notification =
          Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture(context.scope, cleaner, job, %{
            change_summary: "Job moved to 3:00 PM"
          })

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           cleaner: cleaner,
           cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn,
           job: job,
           notification: notification
         })}
      end

      when_ "I tap acknowledge on it", context do
        {:ok, today_live, _html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        today_live
        |> element("[data-test='schedule-alert-#{context.notification.id}-acknowledge-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :today_live, today_live)}
      end

      then_ "the change is marked acknowledged", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.today_live,
                 "[data-test='schedule-alert-#{context.notification.id}']"
               )

        assert has_element?(context.today_live, "[data-test='field-today']")

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "it stops prompting me", context do
        {:ok, today_live, html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        refute html =~ "schedule-alert-#{context.notification.id}"
        assert has_element?(today_live, "[data-test='field-today']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  (`[data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']`) reflects the
  fallback channel used for the re-send.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story842.Criterion7159Spex do
  @moduledoc """

  Criterion 7159 — Checklist opens grouped by room
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner opens her job and sees the checklist grouped by room" do
    scenario "checklist opens grouped by room" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "cleaner Ana is assigned a job with tasks spanning Kitchen, Bathroom, and Living Room",
             context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_room_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner, [
            %{room: "Kitchen", task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
            %{room: "Kitchen", task: "Kitchen floor mopped", required: true},
            %{room: "Bathroom", task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
            %{room: "Living Room", task: "Dust living room shelves", required: false}
          ])

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana opens her job", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}

        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='checklist-room-Kitchen']")
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='checklist-room-Bathroom']")
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='checklist-room-Living Room']")

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "each task appears under its own room, not any other room", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='checklist-room-Kitchen']",
                 "Kitchen counters wiped down"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='checklist-room-Kitchen']",
                 "Kitchen floor mopped"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='checklist-room-Bathroom']",
                 "Bathrooms sanitized"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='checklist-room-Living Room']",
                 "Dust living room shelves"
               )

        refute has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='checklist-room-Bathroom']",
                 "Kitchen counters wiped down"
               )

        refute has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='checklist-room-Kitchen']",
                 "Bathrooms sanitized"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
