defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7153Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7153 — Completing a job generates its invoice
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "marking a job complete generates its invoice" do
    scenario "completing a job generates its invoice" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a scheduled job has an agreed price of $150", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner marks the job complete", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the job is shown as complete to the cleaner", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "an invoice for $150 appears in the owner's billing queue", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices")

        assert html =~ context.client.name
        assert html =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7123 — Cleaner tries to clock in on a job not assigned to them
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner cannot clock in on another cleaner's job" do
    scenario "cleaner tries to clock in on a job not assigned to them" do
      given_ "the owner has an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job is assigned to cleaner Ana, and cleaner Ben also exists", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ben is logged in", context do
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, context.ben)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :conn, conn)}
      end

      when_ "Ben attempts to open Ana's job to clock in", context do
        {:error, {:redirect, %{to: path, flash: flash}}} =

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{redirect_path: path, redirect_flash: flash})}

      then_ "Ben is redirected away with an error explaining the job isn't his", context do

        refute has_element?(ana_job_live, "[data-test='clock-out-button']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

=== 7161_cleaner_completes_a_job_with_a_fully_checked_checklist ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story839.Criterion7161Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 839 — Review photo proof and quality scorecards per job
  Criterion 7161 — Cleaner completes a job with a fully checked checklist
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner checks off every checklist task and completes the job" do
    scenario "cleaner completes a job with a fully checked checklist" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{owner_conn: owner_conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned job with a checklist", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner)

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana checks off every task on the checklist, including the optional one", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        Enum.each(context.checklist.items, fn item ->
          job_live
          |> element("[data-test='checklist-item-#{item.id}']")
          |> render_click()
        end)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      when_ "Ana marks the job complete", context do
        context.job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job is shown as complete to Ana", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees every task checked off when reviewing the job", context do
        {:ok, _review_live, html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/quality/#{context.job.id}")

        for item <- context.checklist.items do
          assert html =~ item.task
        end

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

=== 7163_cleaner_tries_to_complete_with_unchecked_required_tasks ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story839.Criterion7163Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 839 — Review photo proof and quality scorecards per job
  Criterion 7163 — Cleaner tries to complete with unchecked required tasks
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner tries to finish a job while a required task is still unchecked" do
    scenario "cleaner tries to complete with unchecked required tasks" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned job with two required tasks", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner)

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana checks off only one of the two required tasks", context do
        [first_required | _] = Enum.filter(context.checklist.items, & &1.required)

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='checklist-item-#{first_required.id}']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      when_ "Ana tries to mark the job complete", context do
        html =
          context.job_live
          |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
          |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html_after_attempt, html)}
      end

      then_ "the job is not marked complete", context do
        refute render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "Ana is prompted to check off or mark the remaining task skipped with a reason",
            context do
        [_first_required, second_required] = Enum.filter(context.checklist.items, & &1.required)

        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='incomplete-required-tasks-warning']")
        assert context.html_after_attempt =~ second_required.task

        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='skip-task-#{second_required.id}-button']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story839.Criterion7176Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 839 — Review photo proof and quality scorecards per job
  Criterion 7176 — Photo taken offline uploads when signal returns
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a photo captured with no signal finishes uploading once connectivity returns" do
    scenario "photo taken offline uploads when signal returns" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned job with a checklist", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner)

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana captures the required after photo of the first task while her phone has no signal",
            context do
        [task | _] = context.checklist.items

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        upload =
          file_input(
            job_live,
            "[data-test='task-#{task.id}-after-photo-form']",
            :after_photo,
            [%{name: "after_kitchen.jpg", content: "after-photo-bytes", type: "image/jpeg"}]
          )

        render_upload(upload, "after_kitchen.jpg", 40)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job_live: job_live, task: task, upload: upload})}
      end

      then_ "the photo sits queued as a pending upload", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-photo-pending']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "her signal returns", context do
        render_upload(context.upload, "after_kitchen.jpg", 100)

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the photo finishes uploading and is attached to the task", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-photo-pending']"
               )

        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='proof-of-work-photo']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

            :after_photo,

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job_live: job_live, task: task, upload: upload})}
      end

      then_ "the photo sits queued as a pending upload", context do
        assert has_element?(

                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-photo-pending']"

      end

      when_ "her signal returns", context do

        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='proof-of-work-photo']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

""" use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Weekly Schedule <:subtitle>{length(@jobs)} jobs scheduled

That reassignment conflicts with the cleaner's availability or another booking.

{cleaner.name || cleaner.email}

<.job_card :for={job <- jobs_for_cleaner(@jobs, cleaner.id)} job={job} cleaners={@cleaners} />

Unassigned

""" end attr :job, :map, required: true attr :cleaners, :list, required: true defp job_card(assigns) do ~H"""
{@job.scheduled_date} {@job.start_time}-{@job.end_time}
{@job.property.service_address}

    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

defmodule Phoenix.LiveView.Upload do
  # Operations integrating Phoenix.LiveView.Socket with UploadConfig.
  @moduledoc false

  alias Phoenix.LiveView.{Socket, Utils, UploadConfig, UploadEntry}

  @refs_to_names :__phoenix_refs_to_names__

  @doc """
  Allows an upload.
  """
  def allow_upload(%Socket{} = socket, name, opts)
      when (is_atom(name) or is_binary(name)) and is_list(opts) do
    case uploaded_entries(socket, name) do
      {[], []} ->
        :ok

      {_, _} ->
        raise ArgumentError, """
        cannot allow_upload on an existing upload with active entries.

        Consume or cancel the existing entries before allowing a new upload.
        See cancel_upload, consume_uploaded_entry, or consume_uploaded_entries.
        """
    end

    ref = Utils.random_id()
    uploads = socket.assigns[:uploads] || %{}
    upload_config = UploadConfig.build(name, ref, opts)

    new_uploads =
      uploads
      |> Map.put(name, upload_config)
      |> Map.update(@refs_to_names, %{ref => name}, fn refs -> Map.put(refs, ref, name) end)

    Utils.assign(socket, :uploads, new_uploads)
  end

  @doc """
  Disallows a previously allowed upload.
  """
  def disallow_upload(%Socket{} = socket, name) when is_atom(name) or is_binary(name) do
    case uploaded_entries(socket, name) do
      {[], []} ->
        uploads = socket.assigns[:uploads] || %{}

        upload_config =
          uploads
          |> Map.fetch!(name)
          |> UploadConfig.disallow()

        new_refs =
          Enum.reduce(uploads[@refs_to_names], uploads[@refs_to_names], fn
            {ref, ^name}, acc -> Map.delete(acc, ref)
            {_ref, _name}, acc -> acc
          end)

        new_uploads =
          uploads
          |> Map.put(name, upload_config)
          |> Map.update!(@refs_to_names, fn _ -> new_refs end)

        Utils.assign(socket, :uploads, new_uploads)

      {_completed, _inprogress} ->
        raise RuntimeError, "unable to disallow_upload for an upload with active entries"
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Cancels an upload entry.
  """
  def cancel_upload(socket, name, entry_ref) do
    upload_config = Map.fetch!(socket.assigns[:uploads] || %{}, name)

    case UploadConfig.get_entry_by_ref(upload_config, entry_ref) do
      %UploadEntry{} = entry ->
        upload_config
        |> UploadConfig.cancel_entry(entry)
        |> update_uploads(socket)

  def allow_upload(%Socket{} = socket, name, opts)
      when (is_atom(name) or is_binary(name)) and is_list(opts) do
    case uploaded_entries(socket, name) do
      {[], []} ->
        :ok

      {_, _} ->
        raise ArgumentError, """
        cannot allow_upload on an existing upload with active entries.

        Consume or cancel the existing entries before allowing a new upload.
        See cancel_upload, consume_uploaded_entry, or consume_uploaded_entries.
        """
    end

    ref = Utils.random_id()
    uploads = socket.assigns[:uploads] || %{}
    upload_config = UploadConfig.build(name, ref, opts)

    new_uploads =
      uploads
      |> Map.put(name, upload_config)
      |> Map.update(@refs_to_names, %{ref => name}, fn refs -> Map.put(refs, ref, name) end)

    Utils.assign(socket, :uploads, new_uploads)
  end

  @doc """
  Disallows a previously allowed upload.
  """
  def disallow_upload(%Socket{} = socket, name) when is_atom(name) or is_binary(name) do
    case uploaded_entries(socket, name) do
      {[], []} ->
        uploads = socket.assigns[:uploads] || %{}

        upload_config =
          uploads
          |> Map.fetch!(name)
          |> UploadConfig.disallow()

        new_refs =
          Enum.reduce(uploads[@refs_to_names], uploads[@refs_to_names], fn
            {ref, ^name}, acc -> Map.delete(acc, ref)
            {_ref, _name}, acc -> acc
          end)

        new_uploads =
          uploads
          |> Map.put(name, upload_config)
          |> Map.update!(@refs_to_names, fn _ -> new_refs end)

        Utils.assign(socket, :uploads, new_uploads)

      {_completed, _inprogress} ->
        raise RuntimeError, "unable to disallow_upload for an upload with active entries"
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Cancels an upload entry.
  """
  def cancel_upload(socket, name, entry_ref) do
    upload_config = Map.fetch!(socket.assigns[:uploads] || %{}, name)

    case UploadConfig.get_entry_by_ref(upload_config, entry_ref) do
      %UploadEntry{} = entry ->
        upload_config
        |> UploadConfig.cancel_entry(entry)
        |> update_uploads(socket)

## Examples

      assert view
            |> form("#term", user: %{name: "hello"})
            |> render_submit() =~ "Name updated"

  This function is meant to mimic what the user can actually do, so you cannot
   set hidden input values. However, hidden values can be given when calling
   `render_submit/2` or `render_change/2`, see their docs for examples.
  """
  def form(%View{proxy: proxy}, selector, form_data \\ %{}) when is_binary(selector) do
    %Element{proxy: proxy, selector: selector, form_data: form_data}
  end

  @doc """
  Builds a file input for testing uploads within a form.

  Given the form DOM selector, the upload name, and a list of maps of client metadata
  for the upload, the returned file input can be passed to `render_upload/2`.

  Client metadata takes the following form:

    * `:last_modified` - the last modified timestamp
    * `:name` - the name of the file
    * `:content` - the binary content of the file
    * `:size` - the byte size of the content
    * `:type` - the MIME type of the file
    * `:relative_path` - for simulating webkitdirectory metadata
    * `:meta` - optional metadata sent by the client

  ## Examples

      avatar = file_input(lv, "#my-form-id", :avatar, [%{
        last_modified: 1_594_171_879_000,
        name: "myfile.jpeg",
        content: File.read!("myfile.jpg"),
        size: 1_396_009,
        type: "image/jpeg"
      }])

      assert render_upload(avatar, "myfile.jpeg") =~ "100%"
  """
  defmacro file_input(view, form_selector, name, entries) do
    quote bind_quoted: [view: view, selector: form_selector, name: name, entries: entries] do
      require Phoenix.ChannelTest
      builder = fn -> Phoenix.ChannelTest.connect(Phoenix.LiveView.Socket, %{}) end
      Phoenix.LiveViewTest.__file_input__(view, selector, name, entries, builder)
    end
  end

  @doc false
  def __file_input__(view, selector, name, entries, builder) do
    cid = find_cid!(view, selector)

    for entry <- entries do
      content = entry[:content]
      size = entry[:size]

      if content && size && byte_size(content) != size do
        raise ArgumentError, """
        entry content size must match provided size.

        By default the content size is calculated using byte_size/1, so you
        rarely need to provide the size option yourself unless you are testing
        for misbehaving clients.
        """
      end
    end

    case Phoenix.LiveView.Channel.fetch_upload_config(view.pid, name, cid) do
      {:ok, %{external: false}} ->
        start_upload_client(builder, view, selector, name, entries, cid)

      {:ok, %{external: func}} when is_function(func) ->
        start_external_upload_client(view, selector, name, entries, cid)

      :error ->
        raise "no uploads allowed for #{name}"
    end
  end

  defp find_cid!(view, selector) do
    sync_with_root!(view)
    lazy = call(view, {:get_lazy, view.id})

    with {:ok, form} <- DOM.maybe_one(lazy, selector),
         [form] <- DOM.to_tree(form) do
      [cid | _] = DOM.targets_from_node(lazy, form)
      cid
    else
      {:error, _reason, msg} -> raise ArgumentError, msg
    end
  end

  defp start_upload_client(builder, view, form_selector, name, entries, cid) do
    {:ok, socket} = builder.()
    spec = {UploadClient, socket: socket, cid: cid}
    {:ok, pid} = Supervisor.start_child(fetch_test_supervisor!(), spec)
    Upload.new(pid, view, form_selector, name, entries, cid)
  end

  defp start_external_upload_client(view, form_selector, name, entries, cid) do
    spec = {UploadClient, cid: cid}
    {:ok, pid} = Supervisor.start_child(fetch_test_supervisor!(), spec)
    Upload.new(pid, view, form_selector, name, entries, cid)
  end

  @doc """
  Returns the most recent title that was updated via a `page_title` assign.

  ## Examples

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_page_title_update)
      assert page_title(view) =~ "my title"

  """
  def page_title(view) do
    call(view, :page_title)
  end

  @doc """
  Asserts a live patch will happen within `timeout` milliseconds.
  The default `timeout` is [ExUnit](https://ex-unit.hexdocs.pm/ExUnit.html#configure/1)'s
  `assert_receive_timeout` (100 ms).

  It returns the new path.

  To assert on the flash message, you can assert on the result of the
  rendered LiveView.

  ## Examples

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_patch)
      assert_patch view

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_patch)
      assert_patch view, 30

      render_click(view, :event_that_triggers_patch)
      path = assert_patch view

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Money do
  @moduledoc """
  Formats integer cents for display, per the money-handling ADR: every
  amount is stored and computed as integer cents, and this is the only
  place a dollar string gets built.
  """

  @doc """
  Formats integer cents as `"$X.XX"`, with thousands separators. `nil`
  is treated as zero.

  ## Examples

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(18_000)
      "$180.00"

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(nil)
      "$0.00"
  """
  @spec format_cents(integer() | nil) :: String.t()
  def format_cents(nil), do: format_cents(0)

  def format_cents(cents) when is_integer(cents) do
    sign = if cents < 0, do: "-", else: ""
    dollars = div(abs(cents), 100)
    remainder = rem(abs(cents), 100)

    "#{sign}$#{group_thousands(dollars)}.#{pad_cents(remainder)}"
  end

  defp pad_cents(remainder), do: remainder |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")

  defp group_thousands(dollars) do
    dollars
    |> Integer.to_string()
    |> String.reverse()
    |> String.replace(~r/(\d{3})(?=\d)/, "\\1,")
    |> String.reverse()
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure pay calculations — no scope, no `Repo`. Given a job and its
  time entries, this is the only place clocked time (or a fixed piece
  rate) turns into cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry

  @doc "Seconds between clock-in and clock-out. Only meaningful once resolved."
  def worked_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: in_at, clocked_out_at: out_at})
      when not is_nil(out_at) do
    DateTime.diff(out_at, in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed so far on a still-open entry."
  def elapsed_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_out_at: nil, clocked_in_at: in_at}) do
    DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc """
  Cents earned on a job given its (possibly empty) list of time
  entries: the flat piece rate regardless of time for a piece-rate job
  — shown even before the cleaner has started, since it doesn't
  depend on any entry existing — or the hourly rate times total
  resolved worked time. `nil` when an hourly job has no resolved
  entries yet, or a job carries neither pay type: there's nothing to
  compute pay from, and it must not be silently priced at $0.
  """
  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents}, _entries)
      when is_integer(cents) do
    cents
  end

  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: rate}, entries)
      when is_integer(rate) and is_list(entries) and entries != [] do
    if Enum.all?(entries, &TimeEntry.resolved?/1) do
      entries |> Enum.map(&worked_seconds/1) |> Enum.sum() |> hourly_cents(rate)
    end
  end

  def job_cents(_job, _entries), do: nil

  defp hourly_cents(seconds, rate_cents) do
    Decimal.new(rate_cents)
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.div(Decimal.new(seconds), Decimal.new(3600)))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry do
  @moduledoc """
  A single clocked visit to a job: when the cleaner started, and when
  they stopped.

  A `nil` `clocked_out_at` means the entry is open. While the cleaner
  is still on site that's expected and transient; once it's the only
  thing standing between a job and payroll, it's the "missing
  clock-out" the owner must resolve (see
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.resolve_clock_out/3`) before it counts
  toward anyone's pay.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          clocked_in_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          clocked_out_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "time_entries" do
    field :clocked_in_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :clocked_out_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(clocked_in_at clocked_out_at)a

  def changeset(time_entry, attrs) do
    time_entry
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:clocked_in_at])
    |> validate_clock_out_after_clock_in()
  end

  defp validate_clock_out_after_clock_in(changeset) do
    case {get_field(changeset, :clocked_in_at), get_field(changeset, :clocked_out_at)} do
      {%DateTime{} = in_at, %DateTime{} = out_at} ->
        if DateTime.compare(out_at, in_at) == :gt,
          do: changeset,
          else: add_error(changeset, :clocked_out_at, "must be after the clock-in time")

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  @doc "An entry is resolved once it has a clock-out time."
  def resolved?(%__MODULE__{clocked_out_at: nil}), do: false
  def resolved?(%__MODULE__{}), do: true
end

  offline-tolerant upload state.

          upload_state: upload_state(),
          storage_key: String.t() | nil,
          captured_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "photos" do
    field :kind, Ecto.Enum, values: [:before, :after, :incident]
    field :upload_state, Ecto.Enum, values: [:pending, :uploaded], default: :pending
    field :storage_key, :string
    field :captured_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :checklist_item, CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :incident_report, CleanerCrm.Quality.IncidentReport, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(photo, attrs) do
    photo
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :account_id,
      :checklist_item_id,
      :incident_report_id,
      :kind,
      :upload_state,
      :storage_key,
      :captured_at
    ])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :kind])
    |> validate_one_owner()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def uploaded_changeset(photo, storage_key) do
    change(photo, upload_state: :uploaded, storage_key: storage_key)
  end

  defp validate_one_owner(changeset) do
    case {get_field(changeset, :checklist_item_id), get_field(changeset, :incident_report_id)} do
      {nil, nil} ->
        add_error(changeset, :checklist_item_id, "or incident_report_id is required")

      {_id, nil} ->
        changeset

      {nil, _id} ->
        changeset

      {_checklist_item_id, _incident_report_id} ->
        add_error(changeset, :checklist_item_id, "and incident_report_id cannot both be set")
    end

  Nothing here, or anywhere else in this context, updates or deletes
  a report once filed — see the migration's DB rules for the
  backstop, mirroring `CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo

          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,

          filed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          photos: [Photo.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil

    field :description, :string
    field :filed_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    has_many :photos, Photo

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
  end

  @doc """
  `has_photo?` reflects whether a photo accompanies this filing (the
  caller inserts it in the same transaction), since a report needing
  one is judged before any `Photo` row necessarily exists.
  """
  def changeset(report, attrs, has_photo?) do
    report
    |> cast(attrs, [:account_id, :job_id, :cleaner_id, :type, :description, :filed_at])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :job_id, :cleaner_id, :type, :description, :filed_at])
    |> validate_photo_required(has_photo?)
  end

  defp validate_photo_required(changeset, true), do: changeset

  defp validate_photo_required(changeset, false) do
    case get_field(changeset, :type) do
      type when type in @photo_required_types ->
        add_error(changeset, :photo, "is required for this report type")

      _type ->
        changeset
    end
  end

    |> cast(attrs, [:account_id, :job_id, :cleaner_id, :type, :description, :filed_at])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :job_id, :cleaner_id, :type, :description, :filed_at])
    |> validate_photo_required(has_photo?)
  end

  defp validate_photo_required(changeset, true), do: changeset

  defp validate_photo_required(changeset, false) do
    case get_field(changeset, :type) do
      type when type in @photo_required_types ->
        add_error(changeset, :photo, "is required for this report type")

      _type ->
        changeset
    end
  end
end

  A serviced location with address, parking, pet, and access-detail
  notes (entry method, lockbox/alarm codes, emergency contact).

  """

  use Ecto.Schema

  @access_detail_fields ~w(entry_method lockbox_code alarm_code parking_notes pet_notes
                            emergency_contact_name emergency_contact_phone)a

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderScheduler, ReminderSettings}

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :reschedule_requested, reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    case Repo.get_by(Notification, provider_message_id: sid) do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code) when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(%Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification)
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

  def render_hook(view_or_element, event, value \\ %{})

@doc """
  Receives a `form_element` and asserts that `phx-trigger-action` has been
  set to true, following up on that request.

  Imagine you have a LiveView that sends an HTTP form submission. Say that it
  sets the `phx-trigger-action` to true, as a response to a submit event.
  You can follow the trigger action like this:

      form = form(live_view, selector, %{"form" => "data"})

      # First we submit the form. Optionally verify that phx-trigger-action
      # is now part of the form.
      assert render_submit(form) =~ ~r/phx-trigger-action/

      # Now follow the request made by the form
      conn = follow_trigger_action(form, conn)
      assert conn.method == "POST"
      assert conn.params == %{"form" => "data"}

  """
  defmacro follow_trigger_action(form, conn) do
    quote bind_quoted: binding() do
      {method, path, form_data} =
        Phoenix.LiveViewTest.__render_trigger_submit__(
          form,
          :follow_trigger_action,
          "phx-trigger-action",
          "could not follow trigger action because form #{inspect(form.selector)} " <>
            "does not have a phx-trigger-action attribute"
        )

      dispatch(conn, @endpoint, method, path, form_data)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Receives a form element and submits the HTTP request through the plug pipeline.

  Imagine you have a LiveView that validates form data, but submits the form to
  a controller via the normal form `action` attribute. This is especially useful
  in scenarios where the result of a form submit needs to write to the plug session.

  You can submit the form with the `%Plug.Conn{}`, like this:

  defp maybe_values(:hook, _root, _node, _element), do: {:ok, %{}}

  defp maybe_values(type, root, {tag, _, _} = node, element)
       when type in [:change, :submit] do
    cond do
      tag == "form" ->
        value_inputs = DOM.all_value_inputs(node, root)
        defaults = DOM.collect_form_values(node, root, fn defaults -> defaults end)

        lazy_submitter =
          case TreeDOM.attribute(node, "id") do
            nil ->
              # to collect the submitter by selector,
              # need to convert the tree to a lazy here :(
              fn -> DOM.to_lazy([node]) end

            id ->
              # a lazy function that returns a lazy node with all form inputs
              # that could be the submitter to collect the submitter by selector
              fn -> DOM.all(root, ~s<

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Property do
  @moduledoc """
  A serviced location with address, parking, pet, and access-detail
  notes (entry method, lockbox/alarm codes, emergency contact).

  Every property belongs to exactly one client. Lockbox and alarm
  codes are stored encrypted at rest — see `CleanerCrm.Encrypted.Binary`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Encrypted

  @access_detail_fields ~w(entry_method lockbox_code alarm_code parking_notes pet_notes
                            emergency_contact_name emergency_contact_phone)a

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          service_address: String.t() | nil,
          entry_method: String.t() | nil,
          lockbox_code: String.t() | nil,
          alarm_code: String.t() | nil,
          parking_notes: String.t() | nil,
          pet_notes: String.t() | nil,
          client_preferences: String.t() | nil,
          emergency_contact_name: String.t() | nil,
          emergency_contact_phone: String.t() | nil,
          client: CleanerCrm.Clients.Client.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "properties" do
    field :service_address, :string
    field :entry_method, :string
    field :lockbox_code, Encrypted.Binary
    field :alarm_code, Encrypted.Binary
    field :parking_notes, :string
    field :pet_notes, :string
    field :client_preferences, :string
    field :emergency_contact_name, :string
    field :emergency_contact_phone, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @doc """
  Fields whose changes are sensitive enough to warrant an audit entry
  when updated (see `CleanerCrm.Clients.update_property/3`).
  """
  def access_code_fields, do: ~w(entry_method lockbox_code alarm_code)a

  def changeset(property, attrs) do
    property
    |> cast(blank_client_id_to_nil(attrs), [:client_id, :service_address | @access_detail_fields])
    |> validate_required([:client_id, :service_address], message: "is required")
    |> assoc_constraint(:client)
  end

  defp blank_client_id_to_nil(%{"client_id" => ""} = attrs), do: %{attrs | "client_id" => nil}
  defp blank_client_id_to_nil(attrs), do: attrs
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.PropertyFormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create/edit a property with its access details (entry method, lockbox/alarm codes, parking and pet notes, emergency contact). Every property belongs to exactly one client. When the host supplies `client`, the client is fixed (e.g. adding a property from a client's own page) and no picker is shown. When `client` is `nil`, the form renders a client picker and requires a selection. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |-----------------|-------------------------|----------|----------------------------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | | property | `Property.t()` | yes | `%Property{}` (blank for `:new`, loaded for `:edit`) | | client | `Client.t() \\| nil` | yes | preselected client, or `nil` to show the picker | On successful save, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, property}}` to the parent LiveView, which decides where to navigate next. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Clients` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Clients alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header> {form_title(@action)} <:subtitle>Properties carry the access details every job brief inherits. <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="property-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" >

<.icon name="hero-exclamation-circle" class="size-5" />{msg}

<.icon name="hero-exclamation-circle" class="size-5" />{msg}

<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Property
""" end @impl true def update(%{property: property, client: client} = assigns, socket) do changeset = build_changeset(assigns.current_scope, property, client) clients = list_pickable_clients(assigns.current_scope, client) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:clients, clients) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset))} end defp build_changeset(scope, property, nil), do: Clients.change_property(scope, property) defp build_changeset(scope, property, %Client{} = client), do: Clients.change_property(scope, property, %{"client_id" => client.id}) defp list_pickable_clients(_scope, %Client{}), do: [] defp list_pickable_clients(scope, nil), do: Clients.list_clients(scope) @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"property" => property_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Clients.change_property( socket.assigns.property, normalize_params(socket, property_params) ) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end def handle_event("save", %{"property" => property_params}, socket) do save_property(socket, socket.assigns.action, normalize_params(socket, property_params)) end # The client is fixed by the host page, not user-editable — always # trust the assign over whatever the submitted form happens to carry. defp normalize_params(%{assigns: %{client: %Client{} = client}}, params), do: Map.put(params, "client_id", client.id) defp normalize_params(_socket, params), do: params defp save_property(socket, :new, params) do case Clients.create_property(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, property} -> notify_parent({:saved, property}) {:noreply, navigate_to_property(socket, property)} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp save_property(socket, :edit, params) do case Clients.update_property(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.property, params) do {:ok, property} -> notify_parent({:saved, property}) {:noreply, navigate_to_property(socket, property)} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end # Every host routes a saved property to its own page, so the # component can own this navigation directly instead of leaving it # to a parent's `handle_info` — a round trip through a self-sent # message lands one mailbox message after the "save" event's own # reply, too late for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_submit/1` to # observe. Hosts without a router (e.g. isolated component tests) # never call `render_submit` against this path, so the plain # `to:` string is safe even though it isn't router-verified there. defp navigate_to_property(socket, property) do if socket.router do push_navigate(socket, to: "/properties/#{property.id}") else socket end end defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp field_errors(field) do if Phoenix.Component.used_input?(field), do: Enum.map(field.errors, &translate_error/1), else: [] end defp form_title(:new), do: "New Property" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Property" end
